minutes.headline: Assessors heard the tax rate is expected near 1437 per thousand, then spent a long stretch in a heated dispute over the classification hearing.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors met with a new administrative assessing assistant introduced. The principal assessor reported on the classification hearing, interim values approval, the tax billing file now in MUNIS, and abatements. A long, contentious exchange followed over a member's conduct at the hearing and on town meeting articles, then talk of 41C/41D/17D exemptions, Chapter land, and the senior outreach event. Minutes were postponed and the meeting adjourned; no substantive votes were taken beyond adjournment.

budget_items.what_was_said: The principal assessor said the classification hearing went well and the rate looks like it will be about the figure heard, subject to the finance director finishing.
A member noted last year's rate was exactly the figure heard and this year's is subject to change but unlikely to move much.
A member asked about sampling bills at a confidence level; the assessor said checking bills is mainly the tax collector's and finance director's responsibility, with assessors spot-checking.
Board members signed abatement paperwork with the new assistant; totals mentioned.
Members discussed that the finance board's numbers were the only item changing in the hearing slides and that the tax rate is always an estimate until finalized.
Members discussed using a base exemption amount for 41C and resetting income and asset baselines at spring town meeting with COLA thereafter.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors took no substantive votes; approval of the prior minutes was postponed because they had not been revised.
The principal assessor said the classification hearing went well and the FY2025 tax rate should land near the figure heard, pending the finance director.
A long, contentious exchange followed over conduct at the classification hearing and project leadership; it ended with no resolution.
The board set a February 3 senior center outreach conference and an informal timeline for exemption baseline changes ahead of spring town meeting.
The next meeting, December 2, is to review the 41C, 41D, 17D and 22E exemptions and Chapter land applications.

why_it_matters: The tax rate that sets the FY2025 bills was described as an estimate until the finance director finishes, so the final figure on a bill may differ somewhat from the number heard.
Changes to exemption baselines for seniors and others would go to spring town meeting, so residents who claim these exemptions may be asked to vote on them.
